newsitem.title: USA: N.J. says 76 pct of school budgets won approval.
newsitem.headline: N.J. says 76 pct of school budgets won approval.

text.p: New Jersey voters approved 76.2 percent of local school budgets in Tuesday's election, the state's Department of Education said Wednesday.
The department said it was the highest approval rate in the last decade.
In addition, voters in 69.5 percent of districts gave approval to separate ballot questions asking for extra spending beyond state-defined adequacy levels.
Gov. Christine Whitman, who came under fire for school funding reforms in recent months, said the high approval rate showed voters understand the issues.

Whitman's reforms required that each district approve a budget spending a set amount per pupil to meet state minimums. Districts that wanted to spend more on special programs could ask voters for authorization in separate ballot questions.

"Contrary to dire predictions, a large majority, nearly 70 percent of districts with separate ballot questions were approved in their entirety," state Education Commissioner Leo Klagholz said. "As with the base budgets, the decision to support a separate ballot question is one that must be made by a local community dependent on existing conditions."
Voter turnout was 17.8 percent, the department said.
